metadata.title: A Bounded-error Quantum Polynomial Time Algorithm for Two Graph Bisection Problems

extraction_notes.note: The abstract and the Conclusion restate the running-time and success-probability claim of the Introduction; only the Introduction copy (ClP1) is a node.
The paragraph 'It is required to preserve the states ...' in 3.1 repeats AP2's description of the ax_1 entanglement almost verbatim; no separate node, the concrete realization starts at AP4.

algorithm (external, Younes 2013) or a sequence of paper equations: the subsection walks through the cited fixed-phase amplitude amplification in this paper's notation, so it is one external algorithm node containing equations (5)-(11).
Complexity claims are single long sentences that carry their own derivation through several numbered equations; the derivation was left inside the claim rather than split into a proof node.
The complete-graph discussions assert worst-case densities without proof; kept as example/remarks rather than claims because they motivate the adjustments and are not used as results.
Several symbols are introduced in one sentence (psi_c and d_k; d_max and d_min; d_max1, d_max0 and 0-distance; Q, d, z_s, d_s); sentences cannot be split, so each is one definition node.
The Pauli-X gate and the controlled gate Cont_U are defined mid-sentence after equations inside the constraint-evaluation procedure; they stay inside AP5 (sigma_X via its equation EP23).
